title: Undertow and Weather
premise: Isandro Marchetti, night librarian in a city that barely sleeps, has spent five years orbiting her family without ever saying what she knows: that her mother's celebrated life was built on a second name, a hidden marriage, and a half-brother nobody acknowledges. At her mother's funeral, a stranger greets the mourners by that buried surname, and the family's careful architecture of silence begins to crack. As her mother's dementia erases the last living witness, Isandro must choose between the loyalty that held them together and the truth that could free them, finally asking the question everyone arranged themselves around. In the end she learns the name openly from her mother herself—a lucid, deliberate gift—and chooses to keep it not as a secret but as an inheritance, telling her brother on her own terms.
about_author: Felix Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's unopened letters before turning to fiction. They write at night, in libraries, about families who mistake silence for peace.

chapters.title: The Hours We Keep
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Working the night shift in a city that sleeps less every year, Isandro catalogs returned books and rehearses, again, the confession she never delivers to her mother, now fading into dementia. A call from her brother Teo summons her home for the funeral preparations. Emotional beat: the ache of practiced silence, love expressed only through proximity.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the wake, a stranger named Vera offers condolences using the surname 'Marchetti-Aldous'—a name spoken by no one in decades. Teo bristles; their aunt deflects; Isandro recognizes the name from a locked drawer of letters. She follows Vera outside and learns she is the daughter of her mother's first husband. Emotional beat: vertigo—the ground floor of family identity giving way.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Alternating Isandro and Teo POVs. Isandro confronts the aunt with the letters; Teo, whose entire inheritance and identity rest on the official story, accuses her of betrayal at the worst possible hour. Their mother, surfacing briefly from confusion, mistakes Isandro for someone called 'Lena.' Rising tension fractures the family into camps of denial and demand. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized against truth.

chapters.title: Undertow and Weather
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During a storm that floods the library basement, Isandro visits her mother, who surfaces one final time—lucid, deliberate—and tells her the whole story herself, naming Lena as a gift rather than a wound. Isandro chooses not to expose the family publicly but tells Teo privately, on her own terms. He doesn't forgive yet, but he stays. Emotional beat: resolution—truth as inheritance, not detonation; love surviving honesty.
